title: The Smiling House
premise: Dominic Delacroix, a hospice nurse who hears the dying count backwards, inherits Smiling House from an aunt he never met, along with her duty: keep the lights on, count the doors, and never answer when something in the night asks questions. When his sleep recordings capture a second voice answering back, Dominic learns the house is a half-finished ritual vessel built by its founders to harvest souls at each harvest moon, and that his aunt died holding it incomplete. As the moon rises, Dominic must choose between finishing the founders' ritual, which would bind him and everyone he loves to the house forever, or breaking it with the help of Mara, the hospice social worker who refuses to leave his side. He breaks it by answering the house's final question with the truth of his own name, unmaking the founders' power but losing the house and nearly himself; the last chapter finds him and Mara walking away as the building finally goes dark.
about_author: Quentin Crane is the pen name of a former night-shift caregiver who spent six years in residential hospice work before turning to fiction. They write horror about institutions, inheritance, and the things that learn our names.

chapters.title: The Counting
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. In the hospice where he works, patients die counting backwards from numbers they can't explain, and Dominic keeps private tallies of doors and lights to quiet the noise in his own head. A lawyer's letter arrives: Aunt Vivienne Delacroix has left him Smiling House. Emotional beat: dread disguised as opportunity, the first hint that his strangeness is inherited.

chapters.title: Housewarming
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. He arrives at the house with Mara, the hospice social worker who insisted on coming, and finds every light burning, doors numbered in fading paint, and a ledger of rules in his aunt's hand: keep them lit, keep them counted, never answer. The first night, something knocks on a door that isn't there. Emotional beat: uneasy wonder curdling into obligation.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Skeptical of Dominic's rituals, she sets up sleep recordings to prove the house is silent. The playback catches a low voice asking questions through the walls, and worse, a second voice, calm and familiar, answering. She plays it for Dominic without telling him whose voice she thinks it is. Emotional beat: the skeptic's certainty cracking.

chapters.title: Aunt Vivienne's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Hidden pages of the ledger reveal the founders' design: the house is a vessel, the counting a containment, and every Delacroix keeper has fed it small obediences until the harvest moon completes it. His aunt's final entry names him as the intended finisher. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger who loved him enough to trap him.

chapters.title: What the Dying Know
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Back at the hospice, a dying patient grabs Dominic's wrist and counts down to zero, then says his name, a name he's never told anyone there. Mara realizes the house reaches beyond its walls and that the second voice on the tape was Dominic, asleep and answering. Emotional beat: love against duty begins to take shape as she chooses to stay.

chapters.title: The Founders' Circle
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Researching the town archive, he finds photographs of the four founders smiling identically in front of the unfinished house, and a deed clause binding descendants to complete what they started. The house's questions grow more personal, offering him his aunt alive again if he answers. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Doors Out of Count
chapters.summary: POV Mara. The house turns hostile: doors multiply overnight, the count fails, lights die room by room, and Mara is briefly lost in a hallway that shouldn't exist. Dominic finds her by speaking her name aloud, breaking his own rule. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve; they stop pretending they can walk away separately.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Rises
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. On the eve of the full moon, the founders' presence fills the house, and the ritual's final step becomes clear: a keeper must willingly answer the house's last question and surrender their name. His aunt appears in the mirrors, still counting, still holding the door shut from inside. Emotional beat: the weight of inheritance at its heaviest.

chapters.title: Answer Me
chapters.summary: POV Mara, watching. At moonrise the house asks its question, and instead of the founders' scripted surrender, Dominic answers with the truth: who he is, whom he loves, what he owes and refuses. The honest answer is one the ritual cannot hold; the founders' smiles crack, the vessel overfills, and the house begins to consume itself. Emotional beat: climax, love wielded as refusal.

chapters.title: Lights Off
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dawn finds the house dark for the first time in a century, doors all open and equal, the counting finally finished. Dominic hears no backwards numbers anymore, only silence, and grieves the aunt he came too late to know. He and Mara drive away without looking back. Emotional beat: release, mourning, and the quiet cost of being visible at last.
